result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_connected()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if graph is connected. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4017-L4057){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_connected() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Connected components](/assets/graphs/struct-components.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A graph containing three disjoint connected components: a triangle on the left, a two-node edge in the upper right, and a single isolated node in the lower right." width="100%"} A graph is connected if there is a path between every pair of nodes. For directed graphs, checks weak connectivity (treating edges as undirected). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if all nodes are reachable from any node, `False` if the graph has disconnected components. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#a72ea0c0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) graph.is_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Adding a node with no edges gives it no path to the rest of the graph, breaking connectivity: ::: {#6225a3bf .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.add_node(label="D") graph.is_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: :::
